content: To set config values in Gobby's DB-first config store at runtime: PUT http://localhost:60887/api/config/values with {"values": {"key.path": "value"}}. Returns {"ok": true, "requires_restart": true} when a daemon restart is needed.
User preference: Always choose the proper fix over the quick and dirty fix. If it wouldn't pass a code review, don't write it. No shortcuts, no hacks — write code you'd be proud to have reviewed.

The block-escaped-quotes rule blocks Bash commands containing backslash-escaped double quotes in inline scripts. Workaround: write scripts to a temp file using a heredoc with a single-quote delimiter, then run the file. This avoids the escaping pattern that triggers the rule. Use: cat > /tmp/fix.py << 'SCRIPT' ... SCRIPT && uv run python3 /tmp/fix.py

SafeExpressionEvaluator in safe_evaluator.py does NOT support IfExp (ternary: x if cond else y) — or didn't until bafc3d51 added visit_IfExp. Pipeline conditions that use ternary expressions silently fail (ValueError caught by should_run_step, defaults to True). Always test new AST node types if pipeline conditions use Python expressions.

Task MCP lifecycle/status tools now use `TaskToolErrorCode` from `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_errors.py` for workflow-branchable failures. Closed task failures return `error_code: "TASK_CLOSED"`; claim conflicts return `TASK_CLAIM_CONFLICT`; invalid lifecycle statuses return `TASK_INVALID_STATUS`. `build_synthetic_tool_output()` promotes direct MCP `error_code` to top-level `tool_output`, and plan-adversary branches on `tool_output.error_code == "TASK_CLOSED"`.

When syncing bundled DB records that have a UNIQUE index (e.g., agent_definitions with idx_agent_defs_name_scope_project), do NOT use import-then-delete to achieve atomicity — the import will fail with UNIQUE constraint violation because the old record still exists. Instead, use manager.update() for in-place atomic updates, which issues a single UPDATE SQL statement that can't leave the DB in an inconsistent state. The delete-then-import pattern is also risky because if import fails after delete, the old record is permanently lost. The manager.update() approach solves both problems.

When the user asks for analysis, give direct answers to their questions and nothing else. Don't jump ahead to investigating, fixing, or taking action. Answer simply and wait for them to drive the conversation until they're satisfied. Only act when they explicitly ask for action.

CONVENTION: plan-doc revision naming is audit-trail hygiene and applies ONLY when revising a plan AFTER its task tree has already been expanded. When that happens: copy-and-version rather than edit in place. Create `{original-name}-rev1.md` (then `-rev2.md` for subsequent revisions), prepend a change note explaining why the pivot + what the prior design was + date, and leave the original file untouched as the audit trail. Update downstream tasks' `> Plan reference:` lines to point at the latest rev. Does NOT apply during normal drafting before expansion — iterate in place on the original plan file. Rationale (user, 2026-04-21): editing the source plan in place AFTER expansion destroys the link between expanded tasks and the design they were spawned from. Applies to any `.gobby/plans/task-*-plan.md` file that has been expanded into a task tree.

Plan/expand skill content preservation: The plan skill (src/gobby/install/shared/skills/plan/SKILL.md) now uses a heading-based template format (### N.N sections) instead of checklist bullets. Each section's content becomes the subtask description verbatim during expansion. The expand skill (src/gobby/install/shared/skills/expand/SKILL.md) Phase 3 now has anti-summarization rules: TDD header (3-4 lines) + full plan section content below a --- separator. Key principle: the implementing agent only sees its own subtask, so each plan section must be self-contained with file paths, code examples, schemas, and behavioral specs. The /gobby:x invocation syntax was also fixed to /gobby x throughout both files.

rule_engine.py has _clear_edit_write_state(variables) helper that sets edit_write_pending=False and edit_write_stop_blocks=0. Used at 3 sites: circuit breaker tripped, no-rules after_tool success, with-rules after_tool success. Keeps the clearing logic DRY.

SQLite table-recreate pattern in gobby migrations: When adding CHECK constraints (which ALTER TABLE cannot do), use the table-recreate pattern. IMPORTANT: Must disable FK checks with `db.execute('PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF')` before the transaction and re-enable after in a finally block, because LocalDatabase enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` per-connection (database.py:171) and CREATE TABLE with REFERENCES will fail if the referenced table doesn't exist. Also, when patching LocalDatabase in tests, patch at `gobby.storage.database.LocalDatabase` not `gobby.agents.definitions.LocalDatabase` since it's imported locally inside methods.

CLI install flow now builds one LocalDatabase(Path(config.database_path).expanduser()) and one SecretStore(db) in src/gobby/cli/install.py, then passes them through _run_voice_install and _echo_install_summary so the API-key prompts and voice config write never silently fall back to ~/.gobby/gobby-hub.db when the daemon uses a custom database_path.

Don't save memories for plans that haven't been implemented yet. Only save memories for things that are agnostic to the plan — general principles, user preferences, or factual discoveries about the codebase learned while investigating.

Why: In session #3368 (2026-04-22), after tabling a back-half pipeline plan, I saved a project memory describing design decisions from that unimplemented plan (integrator-as-persona, merge halt semantics). Josh rejected: 'I don't want to save memories of plans that haven't been implemented yet. If you learned something agnostic to the plan during your investigation, that's fine.' Unimplemented plans are speculative — they can be rewritten, abandoned, or superseded. Memorializing their design decisions poisons future sessions with 'we decided X' framings for decisions that were never committed to.

How to apply: After tabling or parking a plan, only save memory for content that survives the plan's deletion — durable design principles the user articulated (feedback), codebase facts discovered during research (reference), user preferences (user), or external-system pointers (reference). Do NOT save the plan's design decisions, phase structure, naming proposals, or architectural choices as project memories. When in doubt: would this memory still be useful if the plan were thrown out tomorrow? If no, skip it.

require-task-close rule fix: The stop-gate rule at install/shared/rules/stop-gates/require-task-close.yaml had two bugs. (1) The Jinja template used {{ task_ref }} which is never set in the rule engine's eval context — only in commit_policy.py's context. Fixed to use {{ claimed_task_id[:8] if claimed_task_id else '(unknown)' }} which is available via _build_eval_context() flattening workflow variables. (2) The when condition didn't guard against empty claimed_task_id, causing the rule to fire with blank task IDs. Added `and variables.get('claimed_task_id')` guard.

Pre-existing issue: 14 DB-based tests in tests/workflows/test_task_enforcement_rules.py fail because _sync_bundled() + manager.get_by_name() returns None for all task-enforcement rules (block-native-task-tools, require-commit-before-close, block-skip-validation-with-commit, block-ask-during-stop-compliance, track-task-claim, track-task-release, and require-task-before-edit). The sync function doesn't find rules from the split file structure under task-enforcement/. Only condition evaluation tests (which don't use DB sync) pass.

Task expansion stage selection now lives in src/gobby/tasks/expansion_service.py: `_skipped_stages(task)` parses only resolved `stage-:<name>` labels and ignores `profile:*` sugar, `AUTOMATED_LEAF_CATEGORIES` is {code, config, docs, test}, and dev-only builds complete the expansion run without creating child tasks while setting the parent task lifecycle to in_development. Expansion normalization defaults missing automated leaf agent selection to backend-developer with a `## Agent Selection` marker; task creation now persists assigned_agent/additional_skills.

The gobby web UI has a split styling approach: the chat UI (web/src/components/chat/) uses Tailwind CSS with its own styles.css importing tailwindcss plus additional non-Tailwind styles from the index.css decomposition. All other pages use component-scoped CSS files (e.g., SessionsPage.css, TerminalsPage.css, tasks-page.css) imported by their React components, with shared CSS custom properties (--font-size-base: 16px, --font-mono, --font-sans) and global styles in web/src/styles/index.css (703 lines). index.css was decomposed from 13,849 lines into 16 component-scoped files. When matching styles between chat and non-chat components, map Tailwind classes to their CSS equivalents (e.g., text-xs = 0.75rem, py-1.5 = 0.375rem, px-4 = 1rem).

P2P Agent Infrastructure: AgentCommandManager lives in src/gobby/storage/agent_commands.py. It manages parent-child session commands with lifecycle: pending → running → completed/failed/cancelled. InterSessionMessageManager now has get_undelivered_messages() and mark_delivered() for delivery tracking. LocalSessionManager.is_ancestor() walks parent_session_id chain with cycle guard. Bug #9064: close_task in _lifecycle.py failed to clear task_claimed/claimed_task_id session variables after successful close. Root cause: the claimed_task_id comparison and clearing logic was outside the `if state:` block where claimed_task_id was defined, and the outer `except Exception: pass` silently swallowed any errors. Fix: moved comparison+clearing inside `if state:`, added UUID normalization for robust comparison, replaced silent exception swallowing with logger.warning(). File: src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_lifecycle.py lines ~250-290. The observer fallback in observers.py intentionally does NOT clear for Claude Code (no tool_output in AFTER_TOOL hooks), so CC users are entirely dependent on this MCP proxy clearing code.

Merge agent removed from autonomous dev-loop and orchestrator pipelines (commit c0508c2c). Merge is now manual — the pipeline terminates when all tasks reach review_approved status. The merge agent definition still exists but is not spawned by any pipeline. Reason: pushing to remote and closing tasks autonomously is the highest-risk operation and should be tested on a test project with packaged gobby before enabling. The merge agent also has a no-push conflict with worker-safety rules that needs resolution (push should be an MCP tool, not raw Bash).

Critical bug: If hook_dispatcher.py is deleted or missing while Claude Code hooks are configured, the Stop hook failure creates an infinite loop. Each response triggers the stop hook, which fails and generates a new 'Stop hook feedback' message, which triggers another response, ad infinitum. The only way to break the loop is for the user to Ctrl+C and fix the hook file externally. The agent cannot fix it because PreToolUse hooks also fail, blocking all tool calls. Root cause in this case was unclear — the file existed at ~/.gobby/hooks/hook_dispatcher.py but uv run couldn't find it temporarily (possibly during venv rebuild or daemon restart).

DECISION (2026-04-23): For #12651 skill fetch directives, use the canonical wording `Call get_skill(name="<skill>") on gobby-skills, then continue.` Do not tell agents to pass `session_id` inside get_skill arguments; when Gobby invokes tools through the MCP proxy, session context belongs to the outer call/proxy context, not the inner tool args. Use `loaded_skills` as the replacement ledger for successful agent-visible skill fetches, not `injected_skills`.

The plugin system was removed per the workflows-v2 plan (docs/plans/workflows-v2.md). MCP tools replace plugins as the extension mechanism. However, the removal was incomplete — CLI commands (src/gobby/cli/extensions.py), ClaudePluginsProvider (src/gobby/skills/hubs/claude_plugins.py), and registrations in __init__.py and runner.py still exist. UX convention: All text inputs in the web UI should use Shift+Enter for newline and Enter for submit. This applies to AskUserQuestion 'Other' input, PlanApprovalBar feedback textarea, and any future text inputs. Josh confirmed this is the expected behavior pattern.

The A2UI canvas plan (docs/plans/a2ui-canvas.md) was hardened with CodeRabbit security recommendations in commit 8b61e9fd. Key design decisions: ownership check uses server-side session context (self._get_conversation_id(websocket)) instead of client-provided conversation_id, resolve_interaction uses per-canvas asyncio.Lock for atomicity, WebSocket disconnect cancels pending canvases via cancel_conversation_canvases(), nh3 (not Bleach) for server-side HTML sanitization, three-state optimistic UI flow (active/pending/completed), payload depth validation (max 10 levels) on both backend and frontend. The canvas system is still unimplemented — this is plan-only.

`gobby plans validate <plan-file>` now exists in `src/gobby/cli/plans.py`. It runs the existing Plan-Coverage validator/semantic lint first, then resolves project context with `resolve_project_ref(--project or cwd)` like task CLI commands and runs `consumer_sweep` against local `CodeIndexStorage` when a project id is available. Missing project/index context reports a skipped consumer sweep instead of failing.

Provider context-window resolution now uses config overrides first, ProviderModelCatalog context_length metadata second, and OpenRouter/model_costs as the fallback. ProviderModelCatalog cache version 3 carries context_length, accepts/enriches v2 cache payloads, and handles Claude aliases/canonical IDs, Qwen auth suffixes, and Droid Core provider prefixes.

Gobby worktree create_worktree's hooks_installed response field refers to provider-specific CLI hooks installed via install_provider_hooks(provider, worktree_path), not git hooks. If provider is omitted, install_provider_hooks returns False immediately. Git hooks for worktrees can still be active through shared repo-local core.hooksPath in the common .git/config.

EnterPlanMode and ExitPlanMode are CLI-internal tools in the Claude Agent SDK. They bypass both the can_use_tool permission callback and SDK hooks (PreToolUse/PostToolUse). Neither PreToolUse nor PostToolUse hooks fire for these tools, so they cannot be intercepted via the normal hook system.

Agent run stale-timeout cleanup now keys off child session heartbeat (`sessions.updated_at`) before timing out long-running runs, and timeout persistence backfills `tool_calls_count` and `turns_used` from linked session stats so active work is not mislabeled as a zero-activity timeout.

workflow_definitions table has FK constraint: project_id TEXT REFERENCES projects(id). SQLite FK enforcement is ON (database.py line 171). Tests using project-scoped workflows must create a real project via LocalProjectManager.create() first, then use project.id as project_id. Raw path strings like '/my/project' will cause IntegrityError.

Watchdog circuit breaker state is now persisted to ~/.gobby/watchdog_state.json. The _load_state()/_save_state() methods read/write restart_times as JSON. This means the circuit breaker survives watchdog process restarts — new watchdog instances inherit previous restart counts instead of starting fresh. Tests must mock get_gobby_home during Watchdog construction to avoid loading production state. failure_threshold default changed from 3 to 5.

LLM generate_text max_tokens parameter: Added max_tokens parameter to LLMProvider.generate_text() abstract interface and all 4 implementations (claude, gemini, litellm, codex). For Claude SDK path, max_tokens can't be passed to ClaudeAgentOptions, so post-truncation is used (result[:max_tokens*4]). For LiteLLM/OpenAI paths, it's passed directly to acompletion/create. Default remains 8000 when not specified.

Runner tests formerly in tests/test_runner.py were split for #12255 into tests/test_runner_init.py, tests/test_runner_lifecycle.py, and tests/test_runner_shutdown.py. Shared runner defaults and create_base_patches live in tests/runner_helpers.py; runner fixtures mock_config, mock_config_with_websocket, and fast_stop_hook_grace_window are in tests/conftest.py, with stop-hook patching opt-in via pytestmark usefixtures in runner modules.

Playwright tests for the gobby web UI: The Files page (useFiles.ts hook) now uses relative URLs through the Vite proxy (getBaseUrl returns ''). Use page.route('**/api/files/*') to intercept and mock API calls in tests. Navigation requires opening the sidebar first via .hamburger-button click, then clicking the .sidebar-item. The terminal-colors.spec.ts test is broken because it skips this step. Run Playwright tests from web/ directory: cd web && npx playwright test.

Rules YAML editor save pattern: The web UI YAML editor sends `{ definition: {...} }` to `PUT /api/rules/{name}`. The `RuleUpdateRequest` model must accept this `definition` field, validate it with `RuleDefinitionBody`, extract row-level metadata (description, enabled, priority, tags) into update fields, strip non-body keys (name), and serialize the remainder as `definition_json`. This was fixed in commit c6e289cb.

Bundled content sync architecture (commit 7f7b319b): Five DB-synced content types — skills, prompts, rules, agents, workflows — live in src/gobby/install/shared/{type}/ and sync to SQLite via sync_bundled_content_to_db() in src/gobby/cli/installers/shared.py. This function accepts skip_types: set[str] | None to selectively block types. Dev mode auto-syncs on daemon startup in runner.py (after DB init, before PromptManager/SkillManager). Production mode uses git integrity verification (src/gobby/sync/integrity.py) checking git diff + ls-files on the shared content dirs. The reload_cache MCP tool in workflows/__init__.py now also re-syncs bundled workflows to DB by passing _db to reload_cache(). CLI command: gobby sync with --force/--verify-only/--type/--verbose.

Version numbers are maintained in two places: pyproject.toml (line 3) and src/gobby/__init__.py (line 9). The uv.lock file also contains the version but updates automatically via uv sync. The branch naming convention matches the version (e.g., branch 0.2.22 for version 0.2.22). Merge flow: version branch → dev → main.

Antigravity (VS Code fork) terminal sidebar shows 'tmux' for all terminals by default because `terminal.integrated.tabs.title` defaults to `${process}`. To display tmux window names (set via `set-titles` + `set-titles-string`), change the setting to `${sequence}`. The setting is in `~/Library/Application Support/Antigravity/User/settings.json`. The `set-titles-string` format controls what tmux emits via OSC — consider using just `#W` (window name) for clean sidebar labels instead of the verbose default `#S:#I:#W - "#T" #{session_alerts}`.

Skills refactor — finalized sync model (2026-04-02):

Templates are install artifacts, not runtime sources. DB is always source of truth.

- First install: templates seed DB as source='installed', enabled=True
- Production upgrade: gobby-tagged DB rows updated from new templates (we own them)
- Production: templates are protected/read-only after install
- Dev mode: DB → templates sync (overwrite SKILL.md from DB) so we can maintain templates in source control
- User skills: never gobby-tagged, never touched by any sync
- Drift detection: compares DB against templates, informational
- install_from_template eliminated — bundled skills are directly installed
- project_id scoping stays (already works, no reason to remove)
- SkillTemplatesMixin removed (no more template/installed split in DB)

Bundled items as hidden templates feature: Bundled pipelines/agents/rules (source='bundled' in workflow_definitions table) are now hidden by default in the Workflows UI with a 'Show bundled' toggle. Bundled items never have enable/disable toggles. In dev mode (detected via /admin/status dev_mode field, backed by is_dev_mode()), bundled items get full CRUD. In non-dev mode, bundled items are read-only with 'Use as Template' (creates a custom copy, disables bundled original) and 'Download YAML' actions.

Key backend additions:
- workflow_definitions.py: use_as_template() and use_all_bundled_as_templates() methods
- workflow_definitions.py: get_by_name() now has ORDER BY to prefer custom over bundled
- admin.py: status response includes dev_mode field
- workflows.py: POST /{id}/use-as-template and POST /use-all-bundled-as-templates endpoints
- agents.py: POST /definitions/{name}/use-as-template endpoint

Frontend: showBundled state + devMode fetch from /admin/status in WorkflowsPage.tsx, threaded to RulesTab and AgentDefinitionsPage. CSS: .workflows-card--bundled (dashed border, 0.75 opacity), .workflows-card-badge--template.

Claude Code hook event field names differ between session-start and session-end: session-start uses 'source' (values: 'clear', 'compact', 'startup'), session-end uses 'reason' (values: 'clear', 'logout', 'prompt_input_exit', 'other'). The hook_dispatcher.py confirms this at lines 373-375. The normalization layer (normalization.py) does NOT map between these fields — it only handles tool-related fields.

The Skills page UI was converted from a table/row layout (SkillsTable.tsx) to a card grid layout (SkillsGrid.tsx) matching the Rules page pattern. Key reusable CSS classes from WorkflowsPage.css: .workflows-grid, .workflows-card--template, .workflows-card-badges, .workflows-card-type, .workflows-card-footer, .workflows-toggle*, .workflows-card-actions, .workflows-action-btn/icon. The skill type variant uses .workflows-card-type--skill (sky-blue #38bdf8 on #1a2a3a). Skills now surface source taxonomy (template/installed/project), soft deletes with restore, and scope management (move-to-project/move-to-global) in the UI. The useSkills hook exposes installFromTemplate, moveToProject, moveToGlobal, restoreSkill actions. Note: the backend /skills route does NOT yet accept include_deleted param (only include_templates); the storage layer supports it but the API endpoint needs updating.

Project convention: on-demand skill prompts are intentional, but each skill prompt should fire only once per session. After loading a skill such as brevity, loaded_skills[] should update so the same skill is not requested again in that session.

Uninstall CLI tests (TestUninstallCommand) that test --all or default behavior must monkeypatch Path.home() to a fake_home directory. The uninstall code checks Path.home() for global paths, not CWD. Pattern: fake_home = temp_dir / 'home'; monkeypatch.setattr(Path, 'home', lambda: fake_home); then create .claude/.gemini dirs under fake_home. See tests/cli/test_cli_install.py.

Plan review #13482 round 7 rejected the stage-manifest cutover draft for three blockers: §1.1's plan-prose regression grep self-matches forbidden `copy ... §1.2` wording; §3.1's rule→action→executor boundary only covers a subset of start/advance rules and leaves stale `calls complete_stage` acceptances; §6.1 imports `web/src/lib/stageActions.ts` even though §6.2 creates it later, causing bad sequencing and an undefined shared state type risk.

Never describe an approach as "simplest" or optimize for simplicity. Always choose and present the best, most correct, most complete fix. Rank by correctness and completeness first. Don't mention simplicity as a virtue. If an approach happens to be simple, frame it as "correct" or "complete", not "simple".

Task #13659 split web/src/hooks/useVoice.ts into composing hook plus dedicated voice sub-hooks: `web/src/hooks/voice/useTTSPlayback.ts` owns AudioContext, TTS queueing, pending TTS metadata, binary playback, `stopTTS`, and `isSpeaking`; `useVoiceCapture.ts` owns VAD, PTT recording, WAV encoding, mic cleanup, transcription state, and barge-in callback; `useVoiceStatus.ts` owns `/api/voice/status` polling, warmup prepare, voice mode toggle, and status-derived availability. `useVoice.ts` keeps `UseVoiceReturn`, conversation id/error ownership, conversation-switch cleanup, and `handleVoiceMessage` routing.

Vite dev server (web/vite.config.ts) requires `host: '0.0.0.0'` to be accessible over Tailscale. Without it, Vite defaults to localhost-only binding. The host is now configurable via GOBBY_UI_HOST env var (default: localhost). spawn_ui_server in cli/utils.py sets this env var from config.ui.host. For Tailscale access: set ui.host: 0.0.0.0 in config.yaml. IMPORTANT: Vite 6 also enforces allowedHosts checks when host is 0.0.0.0. The config now sets allowedHosts: true when bound to 0.0.0.0 to allow raw Tailscale IPs (100.x.y.z). Without this, Vite returns a 403/blank page for hosts not matching the allowlist.

API keys in the Gobby codebase resolve from SecretStore (encrypted SQLite, machine-bound via Fernet), NEVER from `os.environ`. User stated this as a project convention.

**Scope:** The convention is canonical for *skill-hub auth resolution* (see task #12053 fix in `src/gobby/mcp_proxy/registries.py:366-372`). The non-hub install prompts at `src/gobby/cli/_install_prompts.py:69-179` still read env for MCP-server keys (GitHub, Linear, OpenAI, Brave, Context7) — that's existing behavior, unclear whether it's intentional or pending cleanup. Don't extend the pattern; do migrate new credential paths to SecretStore-only.

**How to apply:**
- Resolve new hub/provider credentials exclusively through `SecretStore.get(name)`.
- If you see `os.environ.get(<API_KEY>)` in hub/auth resolution code, treat it as a bug to remove.
- Error messages for missing auth should direct users to `gobby install` or `gobby secrets set <NAME>` (value is prompted interactively — never pass it as a CLI argument; `gobby secrets set X VALUE` is not a valid invocation per `src/gobby/cli/secrets.py:44-79`).
- Install-flow prompts for new credentials persist via `SecretStore.set(name, value, category=..., description=...)` with categories in {general, llm, mcp_server, memory, integration}.
- If you need the configured DB path (for `LocalDatabase(...)`), use `load_full_config_from_db()` from `src/gobby/cli/utils.py:23` and pass `Path(config.database_path).expanduser()` — `LocalDatabase()` with no args defaults to `~/.gobby/gobby-hub.db` and silently bypasses custom paths.

Gobby's close_task LLM validator compares the diff against the literal text of validation_criteria — not the spirit. When a reasoned mid-implementation decision diverges from the criteria (directory renames, path shifts, choice-of-approach changes), validation will fail even if the deviation was correct. The recovery path is: (1) update_task(task_id, validation_criteria=<rewritten to match reality>), then (2) close_task(task_id, commit_sha, changes_summary) — re-run normally, no skip.

Do NOT try skip_validation=true with commit_sha. Gobby explicitly blocks that combination with: 'Cannot skip validation when a commit_sha is provided. If you're linking a commit, you did real work — let validation verify it.' The block is intentional: real work must be verified against something rewritten, not bypassed.

Discovered on task #11793 (2026-04-15) when I committed `.upgrade/` after the criteria said `_upgrade/`. The switch was the correct call (dot-prefix dirs are auto-skipped by SkillLoader._load_skill_files at src/gobby/skills/loader.py:658; underscore dirs would have leaked into loaded_files as resources), but the validator couldn't tell from the diff alone.

How to apply going forward: any time a mid-implementation change diverges from the text you wrote at claim time, plan on update_task before close_task. Better still — write validation_criteria at creation time loosely enough that reasonable judgment calls don't require a rewrite: specify *what must be true when done*, not *which exact path or name to use*. If the divergence is too large to rewrite cleanly, escalate_task instead of fighting the validator.

In Gobby, terminal agent child sessions must be expired whenever their agent_run reaches a terminal status (`success`, `error`, `timeout`, or `cancelled`). `LocalAgentRunManager` owns immediate session expiry for terminal status transitions, and `AgentLifecycleMonitor.expire_terminal_run_sessions()` sweeps already-terminal runs so live tmux shells at prompts do not keep Sessions Live entries visible. MagicMock(spec=PydanticModel) does NOT expose Pydantic v2 fields as attributes. Pydantic fields are defined via class-level annotations and __init__, not as class attributes, so mock spec introspection misses them. You must explicitly set field values on the mock: `mock.enabled = True`. This caused 'Mock object has no attribute enabled' errors on MagicMock(spec=WorkflowDefinition) instances.

Hub skill install-on-use is safe because source_type differentiates them from built-in skills. The Cisco skill scanner gate in install_skill blocks HIGH/CRITICAL findings before persisting. SQLite FOREIGN KEY constraints with ON DELETE CASCADE do NOT imply ON UPDATE CASCADE. When migrating/changing a parent row PK, child rows will cause FK violations. Fix: temporarily disable FK checks with PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF (must be outside a transaction), then re-enable in a finally block.

Terminal Spawning (macOS): The Ghostty spawner on macOS injects env vars via shell exports because macOS `open` command doesn't pass env vars to launched apps. In macos.py GhosttySpawner.spawn(), if env vars are provided, they're converted to shell exports and prepended to the command: `exports = " ".join(f"export {k}={v};" for k, v in env.items())` then `shell_cmd = f"{exports} exec {shlex.join(command)}"` with `ghostty_args.extend(["-e", "sh", "-c", shell_cmd])`.

CSS code-splitting gotcha in Vite/React SPAs: When extracting CSS from a monolith index.css into component-scoped CSS files, beware that Vite code-splits CSS alongside lazy-loaded components. If Component A uses CSS classes that were extracted into Component B's CSS file, those styles won't load when only Component A is active.

Specific cases encountered during index.css decomposition:
1. `.conversation-picker` styles were in SessionsPage.css but used by ChatPage — moved to chat/styles.css
2. `.session-item`, `.session-group` shared primitives were in TerminalsPage.css but used across chat/sessions/terminals — moved to index.css (always loaded)
3. `.workflows-*` layout classes in WorkflowsPage.css used by SkillsPage.tsx — added WorkflowsPage.css import to SkillsPage.tsx
4. `task-execution.css` import was missing after Activity Panel tabs were refactored — fixed in commit 67024049
5. `files-code-viewer` and `files-tree-*` CSS rules were in FilesPage.css but needed by Chat UI file tree — extracted to chat/styles.css to decouple Chat UI styling from FilesPage.css and enable reuse of file tree styles across different contexts.

Rule of thumb: styles for classes used across multiple code-split boundaries must be in a globally-loaded CSS file (index.css or main.tsx import) or imported by all consuming components. When CSS breaks during component restructuring, check for missing stylesheet imports first.

Investigation: Expander Agent Replacing Task Decomposition (#8943)

## Key Finding: Expansion is Already Skill-Driven

The old expansion.py (TaskExpander) has been REMOVED. Current architecture:
1. Skill (expand/SKILL.md, 458 lines): Instructs AI agent to analyze codebase, generate spec, create subtasks
2. MCP Tools (_expansion.py): save_expansion_spec, execute_expansion, get_expansion_spec
3. Flow: Agent reads task -> analyzes codebase (Glob/Grep/Read, visible) -> generates spec -> saves -> executes atomically
4. Compaction recovery: save_expansion_spec persists spec to DB, get_expansion_spec detects pending for resume

## Assessment: Dedicated Agent Has Questionable Value

Current skill approach advantages:
- Conversation visible to user (transparency, debugging)
- Uses existing session context (codebase knowledge)
- No spawn latency
- Interactive (user can guide decomposition)
- Session compaction recovery via save/resume

Dedicated agent approach would add:
- Isolated context (won't pollute session) 
- Parallel execution capability
- But: loses interactivity, visibility, existing context, adds spawn latency

## Recommendation: Keep Skill-Based, Enhance with Rules

Rather than spawning a dedicated agent, add expansion quality rules:
- before_tool on save_expansion_spec: validate subtask count (warn if <2 or >15)
- Validate description length (warn if any subtask <50 chars)
- Validate TDD compliance (check code/config tasks have TDD headers)
- Validate dependency graph (warn on circular deps)

This gives enforcement benefits without dedicated agent complexity. The expansion is already agent-driven — the skill IS the agent behavior, just running in the current session.

Feasibility of dedicated agent: MODERATE technically, LOW value proposition.
When changing Gobby tool-call JSON rendering, preserve colored syntax highlighting for arguments/results; wrapping long JSON should not downgrade those renderers to plaintext <pre> output.

Design token gotcha: --accent-foreground is the foreground color paired with bg=--accent (chartreuse). It is theme-flipping (near-black in dark, near-white in light). NEVER use it as a generic high-contrast text token. It only renders correctly when the background is also paired-flipping in the same direction (--accent, --color-error, --color-success-foreground, etc.). When the background is fixed-bright in both themes (e.g., PROVIDER_COLORS hex literals from sourceTheme.ts) or absent (inline SVG with currentColor), light-mode text becomes near-white-on-bright = invisible. Two real bugs found and fixed in commit 312cf65c8: (1) .source-icon-codex inline SVG, (2) .agent-def-badge--filled. Rule for review: any color: var(--accent-foreground) without a sibling background: var(--accent) (or var(--color-error|warning|success|*-foreground)) in the same rule is a contrast bug.

Neo4j auth secrets architecture: During onboarding (Ink setup wizard), the DB doesn't exist yet, so secrets can't be stored in the encrypted SecretStore. The pattern is: (1) store plaintext in setup_state.json or config.yaml during install, (2) after daemon starts and DB is created, migrate plaintext secrets to the encrypted SecretStore using ConfigStore.set_secret() which stores '$secret:NAME' reference in config_store and encrypted value in secrets table. The SecretStore uses Fernet encryption tied to machine identity (PBKDF2 key from machine_id + salt). Pattern: $secret:neo4j_auth in config → resolved at load time via secret_resolver callback.

Hook system architecture: Rules evaluate ONCE centrally in hook_manager.handle() via workflow_handler.handle() -> evaluate(). The fix made handle() return evaluate() directly, preserving mcp_call metadata for dispatch. The _evaluate_workflows method was removed from EventHandlersBase.

Chrome's getComputedStyle().getPropertyValue('--my-token') returns the declared value unchanged for oklch()/lab()/color() — it does NOT normalize to rgb. Setting canvas ctx.fillStyle = 'oklch(...)' and reading it back also returns the oklch string unchanged in Chromium. The reliable way to convert any CSS color (including oklch) to actual sRGB is to *paint* it: ctx.fillRect(0,0,1,1) then ctx.getImageData(0,0,1,1).data — the painted pixel is rasterized to sRGB. Used in web/src/lib/utils.ts resolveCssVar() for the 3D force-graph (#13656) so three.js / SpriteText consumers get rgb(r,g,b) regardless of whether the design token is declared in oklch.

Every CLI adapter in src/gobby/adapters/ must be standalone — no cross-CLI inheritance. Each adapter extends BaseAdapter directly, never another adapter (e.g. no DroidAdapter(ClaudeCodeAdapter) even when their hook protocols look identical).

Why: Coding CLIs diverge over time. Factory, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and Qwen ship hook-format and transport changes independently. Coupling two adapters via inheritance turns every upstream change into a coordinated-update problem. The user was explicit during planning for the droid adapter: 'every CLI gets its own adapter. coding agents diverge. we can't depend on the CLIs staying in sync.'

How to apply: When adding a new CLI adapter, pattern-match on the closest existing one for structure but copy the code into a new file. Expect ~100–500 lines of duplicated plumbing; that's correct. Shared logic belongs in BaseAdapter or in src/gobby/hooks/ (event handlers are already CLI-agnostic), not in cross-adapter inheritance. Same rule applies to transcript parsers in src/gobby/sessions/transcripts/ and installers in src/gobby/cli/installers/.

Step workflow enforcement is wired into rule_engine.py's evaluate() method at two points: (1) BEFORE_TOOL — _check_step_tool_enforcement() checks allowed_tools/blocked_tools and allowed_mcp_tools/blocked_mcp_tools from the current WorkflowStep, returning a block HookResponse if disallowed. Skills should teach when/how/why, not duplicate what progressive discovery provides. Skills that enumerate MCP tools and their schemas go stale by design — every time a tool is added or changed, the skill becomes outdated. Progressive discovery handles 'what tools exist and what params do they take.' Skills should focus on: decision frameworks (when to use X vs Y), behavioral patterns (how to do it well), judgment calls (why this matters), and anti-patterns (what to avoid). API reference in skills is an anti-pattern.

plan-adversary has a state-machine deadlock on reject verdicts in the interactive /gobby plan path (observed 2026-04-22, filed as task #12617):

1. /gobby plan Step 7.1 creates the per-attempt planning epic with default status=open.
2. spawn_agent(agent='plan-adversary') auto-claims → status=in_progress.
3. When the adversary decides REJECT and calls mark_task_review_rejected, the transition guard fails because it requires source status = needs_review (the rejection verb moves needs_review → open).
4. mark_task_needs_review is in plan-adversary.yaml's `blocked_mcp_tools`, so the adversary cannot unblock itself.
5. The adversary's workflow terminate step still fires (result.status=success) but NO verdict is persisted — no rejection_notes appended, no status transition, task stuck in_progress claimed by the dead child session.
6. The only place the verdict survives is the Codex rollout transcript at ~/.codex/sessions/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/rollout-*.jsonl (grep for 'mark_task_review_rejected' + 'rejection_notes').

The autonomous front-half likely sidesteps this by creating planning tasks directly in needs_review state (or skipping claim_task). Interactive /gobby plan does not, so interactive adversarial reject loses findings silently.

Workaround until #12617 lands: if an adversary run completes with status=success but the planning task has no `## Adversary Findings — Round N` heading, the verdict almost certainly bounced — recover findings from the Codex rollout (filename timestamp is LOCAL time, not UTC; match on content or on mtime in the session window).

Bug pattern: add_dependency(task_id, depends_on) uses positional args where task_id is the dependent and depends_on is the blocker. Match infrastructure investment to scope — never land 30% of a refactor.

When planning a feature, the size of the infra change has to match the size of the feature. If scope is narrow (one or two call sites, one surface), use existing side channels — the `metadata` JSON blob, config files, Python filtering in the handler — and skip schema migrations, new columns, and new model fields.

Why: In session #3187 on task #12058 (`internal: true` skill flag), the user rejected my first plan because it added a schema migration + dedicated `skills.internal` column + `Skill` dataclass field for a feature that only hid two skills from one MCP tool surface. Their framing: 'we could just simplify it by adding it to the metadata. you're not wanting to do the full conversion which tells me this needs to be a deeper epic rather than a halfass task.' Half-landing a migration (without follow-through on every listing surface or an audit of all candidate skills) is worse than not landing one at all — it creates dead infra that invites confusion later.

How to apply: Before planning, ask: does this touch 2 call sites or 20? One surface or every surface? If narrow, propose the minimal version (metadata blob, Python filter) and create a follow-up epic capturing what the full conversion would look like (e.g. #12075 blocks #12058). If wide, propose the full conversion. Never propose a plan that does 30% of a proper refactor — it reads as half-assed and will get rejected. When uncertain, describe both options, flag which you'd pick, and let the user decide.

runner_maintenance.py zombie cleanup pattern: The cleanup_zombie_messages_loop function expires undelivered inter-session messages to dead sessions. Key design points: (1) SQL must handle both ended_at < threshold AND ended_at IS NULL with started_at fallback, since crashed sessions never set ended_at. (2) The loop runs cleanup once immediately on startup before entering the sleep loop, so zombies from before a daemon restart don't wait a full interval. (3) The cleanup is extracted into a _expire_zombies() inner function to avoid duplication between the startup call and the loop body.

Workflow variable evaluation architecture: `variables.get()` in session-lifecycle.yaml `when` expressions is architecturally correct. The `variables` dict is a merged dict combining workflow state variables AND session variables, with session_variables having override priority. The `session` object in eval context is a Session DB record (id, status, branch metadata), NOT a variables container. Do NOT replace variables.get() with session.* - this would break all workflows. The set_variable workflow action persists to workflow_states.variables, and the MCP set_variable tool persists to session_variables table. Both are loaded and merged before evaluation.

Context window usage calculation: The context window (e.g. 200k for Claude) is an INPUT limit. Output tokens do NOT occupy it. Correct formula: context_load = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens. Percentage = context_load / context_window. Output tokens should be shown separately in tooltips but never added to the numerator. The DB field usage_input_tokens stores the total (uncached + cache components), so when hydrating uncachedInputTokens for display, compute: total - cache_read - cache_creation.

When adding scope columns to a DB table for the DB-first pattern (bundled/global/project), the create() method must auto-infer scope='project' when project_id is provided and scope is the default 'global'. Without this, existing callers that pass project_id without explicit scope will create records with scope='global', breaking the SQL scope precedence query (ORDER BY CASE scope WHEN 'project' THEN 1...).

Sentence collision fix in websocket/chat.py: The has_sent_text flag tracks whether any text was sent in the current turn, independent of accumulated_text flushes. The fix uses `has_sent_text` which survives the flush.

YAML `>` folded scalar pitfall: Lines with MORE indentation than the first content line preserve the preceding newline instead of folding it to a space. This caused a critical bug in command-mcp-tool-restriction where `not in` on an extra-indented line produced `...)
  not in ...` — a SyntaxError in ast.parse(mode='eval'). Because _evaluate_condition in rule_engine.py uses fail_closed=True for block effects, the SyntaxError defaulted to blocking ALL tools unconditionally. Fix: (1) keep all continuation lines at same indent in YAML `>` blocks, (2) SafeExpressionEvaluator._normalize_expr() now collapses whitespace before parsing as defense-in-depth.

Fix for debug_echo_context persisting after YAML change: Changing debug_echo_context from true to false in workflow YAML (e.g., claude-sdk-lifecycle.yaml) does NOT take effect for existing sessions because persisted workflow state variables take precedence over YAML defaults. Fix: use set_session_variable(name="debug_echo_context", value="false", session_id="#N") via gobby-workflows MCP server. Session variables (_session_variables_override) have highest precedence per evaluate_all_lifecycle_workflows. New sessions inherit the YAML default. The duplicate [DEBUG additionalContext] injection was caused by the debug echo re-injecting the same additionalContext as a system_message with prefix.

FastAPI test patterns learned during coverage push:

1. isinstance with lazy imports: When route handlers do `from gobby.storage.database import LocalDatabase; isinstance(db, LocalDatabase)`, MagicMock fails. Fix: autouse fixture patching `gobby.storage.database.LocalDatabase` with `MagicMock` class so isinstance(MagicMock(), MagicMock) returns True.

2. Test directory naming conflicts: Never name a test directory after a Python package (e.g., tests/servers/routes/mcp/ clashes with the `mcp` package). Use `mcp_endpoints/` instead.

3. FastAPI dependency_overrides: Routes using Depends(get_server) need `app.dependency_overrides[get_server] = override_fn` instead of `create_X_router(mock_server)` pattern.

4. Exception re-wrapping: If a route catches HTTPException(503) inside a generic `except Exception`, it re-raises as 500. Check the actual handler logic when writing test assertions.

5. Installer backup-before-read order: copy2 (backup) runs before open (read), so making a file unreadable causes 'Failed to create backup' not 'Failed to read'.

React useCallback stale closure pattern in Gobby web UI: when an async handler inside useCallback references state (like graphData) and also appears in the dependency array, two problems occur: (1) the callback recreates on every state change causing unnecessary re-renders, and (2) if the async operation completes after state changes, it merges with stale data. Fix: use functional state updates — setGraphData(prev => prev ? mergeGraphData(prev, data) : data) — which removes the state from the dep array and always uses current state. Applied in KnowledgeGraph.tsx handleNodeClick.

Neo4j entity-memory linkage: Entities in Neo4j get a common _Entity label (via SET after MERGE to avoid mismatch). When memories are created, entities are linked to (:Memory {memory_id}) nodes via MENTIONED_IN relationships. This enables graph-augmented search: vector search finds entities, MENTIONED_IN links resolve to memory IDs, and graph traversal finds related memories. Backfill via rebuild_knowledge_graph MCP tool passes memory_id to add_to_graph().

ChatInput button layout fix (ChatInput.tsx): Replaced conditional streaming/non-streaming button blocks with a single stable container using 'flex gap-1 shrink-0'. This prevents the bar from growing vertically when buttons appear/disappear. Send stays enabled during streaming to allow interrupt-with-message.

React 18 error boundary limitation: Error boundaries only catch errors during rendering, lifecycle methods, and constructors. They do NOT catch errors in event handlers, async code (setTimeout, requestAnimationFrame, promises). Three.js render loops use requestAnimationFrame, so WebGL crashes bypass error boundaries entirely. When no error boundary catches a render error in React 18, the ENTIRE root tree is unmounted (different from React 17 which left corrupted tree mounted).

BUG: pending_memory_review stop gate is unresettable via MCP set_variable. Root cause: workflow YAML set_variable action writes to workflow_states.variables, but MCP set_variable tool writes to session_variables table (because session_var_manager takes priority in _variables.py:124-126). The lifecycle evaluator (lifecycle_evaluator.py:621-623) only reads from workflow_states.variables, never session_variables. So the MCP call writes to the wrong store. Fix: merge session_variables into context_data in the lifecycle evaluator around line 618, so both stores are visible to when-clause evaluation.

React TSX gotcha: When using `obj?.field && (<JSX>)` pattern in JSX conditional rendering, if the type of `field` is `unknown` (e.g. from a Record<string, unknown>), TypeScript errors with 'Type unknown is not assignable to type ReactNode'. Fix by using `!!obj?.field && (<JSX>)` to coerce to boolean. This is because JSX conditional `{x && <Foo/>}` requires `x` to be a valid ReactNode when truthy, and `unknown` doesn't satisfy that constraint.

WorkflowHookHandler serializes per-session rule evaluation with a threading.Lock registry acquired from async code. This is intentional because evaluate() can enter _evaluate_rules through sync bridge paths and different event loops; a shared asyncio.Lock would be unsafe under cross-loop contention. SESSION_END cleanup is ref-counted so queued same-session hook events keep using the same lock until all waiters drain.

Gobby tmux sessions use an isolated socket (`-L gobby`). ## Agents v3 Design Decisions (Epic #9085)

### Core Concepts
- **Selectors**: Compact string syntax for targeting rules by metadata — `tag:X`, `group:X`, `name:X`, `source:X`, `*`. Fnmatch globs. Include is OR, exclude wins on conflict. No boolean combinators in v3.
- **`extends`**: Single inheritance for agent definitions. Child overrides parent. Max depth 5, cycle detection. Uses Pydantic `model_fields_set` to detect explicit overrides vs defaults.
- **`inherit`**: Sentinel value for provider/model. Resolved from CLI source at session_start or spawn time via `_CLI_SOURCE_TO_PROVIDER` map.
- **`mode: self`**: "Persona, not process." Loads rules+variables onto current session without spawning. Already exists in spawn layer but not in `AgentDefinitionBody.mode` Literal. Being added as first-class + decoupled from requiring a workflow.
- **`default_agent`**: New `DaemonConfig` field (default: "default"). Deep loaded at session_start in `handle_session_start` — before rules evaluate. Writes `_agent_type`, `_active_rule_names`, preset variables to `session_variables`.
- **`_active_rule_names`**: New session variable. When set, rule engine filters to only these rule names (via `_filter_by_active_rules`). When None, all rules pass (backward compat).

### Key Architecture
- New files: `src/gobby/workflows/selectors.py`, `src/gobby/workflows/agent_resolver.py`
- Injection point: `src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_session.py` handle_session_start, after session registration, before rules evaluate
- Rule engine change: `_filter_by_active_rules` added after `_filter_by_agent_scope` in evaluate()
- Spawn evolution: `_modes.py` gets `_handle_self_persona` for workflow-less mode:self
- Agent sync already exists at `src/gobby/agents/sync.py`

### Phase 2: Variable Definitions
- First-class `workflow_type='variable'` in `workflow_definitions` table (no schema change)
- Replaces 14 session-defaults rules (all pure set_variable initializers guarded by `is None`)
- 6 conditional set_variable rules in other groups stay as rules
- User chose first-class variable registry over variables-as-rule-outputs

### User Preferences
- User wants `mode: self` (not terminal/headless) for the baseline agent concept
- User prefers config setting for default agent activation (not convention-based)
- User wants deep load pattern (like session ID) for agent activation at session_start
- Keep straightforward for agents v3 — no boolean combinators, no compound selectors

Python import gotcha: When `gobby.cli.__init__.py` has `from .setup import setup`, the `setup` attribute on `gobby.cli` becomes the Click Command object, shadowing the `setup` submodule. In tests, `import gobby.cli.setup as setup_mod` resolves to the Command, not the module. Fix: use `importlib.import_module('gobby.cli.setup')` to get the actual module for monkeypatching. This applies to any CLI module where __init__.py re-exports a same-named symbol.

Don't use skip_validation on close_task unless there's a genuine reason (e.g. validator can't see the diff, truncated context). Web UI accent usage rule (deutan-safe palette, brand chartreuse oklch(82% 0.20 125) dark / oklch(50% 0.18 125) light): solid `bg-accent` is too punchy for any non-CTA surface. Use it only for genuine call-to-action buttons (Send, primary submit), tiny status indicators (dots, focus rings), and active-state highlights on small surfaces. For tab triggers, panel headers, type/state badges, and any background fill on >32px-tall element, use `bg-secondary` with optional accent border, `var(--accent-tint)` (10% opacity overlay), or a token from the state palette (warning amber, info blue, magenta error). The Phase 1 colorize tokens are correct; the gap is component-level overuse of the solid accent.

**Why:** Verified live in browser across desktop+mobile, dark+light. Activity panel `bg-accent` headers, Live pill, and action buttons all read as electric chartreuse slabs that dominate the layout and undermine the 'calm but dense' design principle from .impeccable.md.

**How to apply:** During Phase 2 component sweep (#13416), every `bg-accent` occurrence outside a primary CTA button is a code smell. Default to `bg-secondary` + accent text/border; promote to solid only when it's clearly the most important action on screen.

When using generic retry helpers that take an async callable (lambda) in Python 3.13, Mypy may fail to infer the type of the lambda, resulting in [misc] errors. Placing `# type: ignore[misc]` on the same line as the lambda definition resolves this issue.

MCPClientManager now treats single-server list_tools discovery failures as stale-session candidates: it records the failure, discards and best-effort disconnects the cached connection, reconnects once via ensure_connected, retries list_tools, and raises MCPError with normalized original/retry errors if retry fails. MCPClientManager.disconnect_all finalizes connection, health, reconnect task, and lazy connection state under cancellation without re-raising cancellation from teardown cleanup.

Block observability uses structured logs in owned Gobby paths with the format `BLOCK session=<id> event=<type> tool=<name> source=<rule|step-enforcement|webhook|session-lifecycle> rule=<name> reason=<text>`. Claude Agent SDK's ResultMessage.usage accumulates token counts across ALL API calls within an agentic turn (not per-call). For a turn with N tool calls, cache_read_input_tokens ≈ N × context_size, easily exceeding the context window. To get accurate per-call usage, enable include_partial_messages=True on ClaudeAgentOptions, then capture message_start StreamEvent objects — their usage dict contains the actual per-call input token counts. Use the LAST message_start's usage for context % calculation. StreamEvent is imported from claude_agent_sdk.types (not the top-level package). Fixed in chat_session.py and claude_streaming.py.

Watchdog restart loop root cause: daemon startup sync (skills, prompts, workflows, agents, task import) takes ~35s before the HTTP server binds. The watchdog restart_daemon() was only waiting 13s for health checks, so it kept killing and restarting. Fixed in #8798 by increasing to 55s. Key diagnostic: watchdog.log shows repeated 'Daemon started but not responding to health checks' + 'Restart attempt failed', while gobby.log shows sync tasks completing but no HTTP bind. The sync tasks repeat every ~35s in the log because each watchdog-killed restart starts them over.

runner.py Phase 2 config reload bug: The second load_config() call (with config_store) didn't pass config_file, so when the DB config_store was empty (fresh installs, e2e tests), DaemonConfig(**{}) returned all defaults (daemon_port=60887, default DB path). `mark_task_review_rejected` accepts both `needs_review` and `in_progress` states. Interactive planning/adversary flows can auto-claim a review task before emitting a reject verdict, so rejection must still persist findings, clear ownership, and reopen the task.

Chat UI off-by-one bug after interrupt: When a user sends a new message while the previous response is streaming, the Claude SDK's response buffer isn't fully drained after interrupt(). The next receive_response() call returns stale events from the interrupted query, and _stream_chat_response tags them with the NEW request_id — so the frontend renders the old response as if it belongs to the new message. Fix: Added drain_pending_response() to ChatSession (chat_session.py) that consumes remaining events after interrupt, and call it in _cancel_active_chat (websocket/chat.py) after task cancellation.
